tagline: Oldest stone Buddhist structure in India with carved gateways.

sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, on a hilltop in Raisen district near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, is the oldest surviving stone structure of its kind in India and one of the most important Buddhist monuments in the world. The original brick stupa was commissioned by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. It was later enlarged and covered with stone in the 2nd century BCE, and four ornate gateways, the toranas, were added in the 1st century BCE under the Satavahanas. Sanchi remained an active Buddhist centre for more than a thousand years.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of the Great Stupa lies in its clear form and its carvings. A solid hemispherical dome, about 36 metres in diameter, rises from a circular base surrounded by a stone railing and a walkway used for ritual circumambulation. The four toranas, each covered with detailed relief carvings, are the highlight. They illustrate stories from the Buddha's life and his previous births, the Jataka tales, and show lively scenes of people, animals, trees and royal processions. In early Buddhist art, the Buddha is not shown in human form but represented by symbols such as the wheel, the footprints, the empty throne and the Bodhi tree.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: Other monuments on the hill add to the importance of the site. Stupa 2 and Stupa 3 are smaller but also finely decorated, and Stupa 3 contained relics said to be of two of the Buddha's chief disciples. An Ashokan pillar carries an inscription in the Brahmi script. There are also ruins of monasteries and a Gupta-period temple, which show the long span of occupation.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: The site was rediscovered in 1818 and restored in the early 20th century under the archaeologist John Marshall. The Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989. They are famous for their harmony of design and symbolism.

visitor_tips: Visitors should plan two to three hours, ideally in the morning or evening for the best light.
A small museum displays finds from the site.
Nearby are the Udayagiri Caves, Vidisha and Bhopal.
